health.shortComment: For now, Maye -- who suffered a fractured right fibula during a Week 10 loss to the Lions -- remains on the Patriots' 53-man roster rather than injured reserve, with coach Mike Vrabel citing the "balance" the team is hoping to strike with regard to managing its remaining designated to return from IR slots, Mike Reiss of ESPN.com reports.
health.longComment: Per Reiss, teams are limited to eight players that can be designated to return from the list over the course of the regular season, and the Patriots are close to using them all. "Right now, he's not on injured reserve," Vrabel said Monday. "He's on the active roster, so that's where it is today. I think that those things are obviously fluid. But we want to try to give him every opportunity that we can to be back at some point in time. I don't know when that will be; I'm not sure. But also, try to manage the roster and do what we need to do to try to win each week." On Sunday, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reported that Maye was on track to miss at least six weeks, a timetable that suggests, in a best-case scenario, the QB could make a push for a late-season return or for the postseason, should New England qualify. Heading into a Week 12 game against the Chargers, Tommy DeVito is slated to work as the team's starter, with rookie Behren Morton on hand as his backup. Additionally, there's the possibility that the team considers Daniel Jones -- who the Colts let go Friday -- as an alternative, but Vrabel told Reiss that in the short term at least, adding another signal-caller is not something that's being planned.
factors: Officially ruled Out on weekly game status report

health.irBeatNote: Henderson was already ruled out for Sunday's game against the Lions in Munich, and now that he's on IR, the second-year running back will be required to miss at least the next four games. Henderson's next opportunity to play is Week 15 against the Chiefs on Monday, Dec. 21, although there's no timetable for his return, as he is recovering from "an unexpected and unusual medical emergency involving a series of neurological symptoms." If Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) cannot play Sunday, then the Patriots' backfield will be led by Corey Kiner and Lan Larison.
health.shortComment: Henderson (illness) was placed on injured reserve Saturday, Mike Reiss of ESPN.com reports.

health.longComment: Rouse is in the league's concussion protocol, which prevented him from playing in Week 10 against the Lions in Munich. Despite the extra rest courtesy of the Week 11 bye, the third-year pro has not progressed enough in his recovery to return to practice. Even if he practices over the coming days, an independent neurologist would need to clear Rouse from protocol in order for him to be available for Sunday's game against the Chargers.
factors: Remains in early stages of NFL 5-Step Concussion Protocol
